gym.landing.how.title: Log the set. The rest is remembered.
gym.landing.how.sub: Three beats, in the order they happen at the rack.
gym.landing.how.logCopy: Two taps between sets. Big targets for one thumb and chalked hands — the small step is the 2.5 kg your program is written in, the big one is a plate change.
gym.landing.how.rememberCopy: Next session opens with last time’s numbers already in the field. You never scroll back to find what you lifted.
gym.landing.how.lineCopy: e1RM per lift, week over week — the long line of showing up. A PR gets one line.
gym.landing.how.ladderCaption: the small step is your program step · the big one is a plate change
gym.landing.how.lineCaption: 137.5 → 140 · one quiet line for a PR
gym.landing.barbell.title: Built for the barbell
gym.landing.barbell.sub: Squat, bench, deadlift, press, rows — e1RM per lift, week over week. e1RM is estimated one-rep max (Epley: weight × (1 + reps/30)).
gym.landing.barbell.example: Example: twelve weeks of a linear cycle. Chins here carry no added load, so Epley has no answer for them — they are drawn on the reps of the top set instead, and no estimate is invented over a bodyweight the log does not hold.
gym.landing.connected.title: Your log is an endpoint your own AI tools can use.
gym.landing.connected.sub: The log is free — all of it, and so are these tools. So is Coach, the room in the app for a lifter who hasn’t got an agent of their own — ten questions a day, and nothing in Gym is on sale.
gym.landing.connected.canRead: Read your last twelve weeks of squats.
gym.landing.connected.canPropose: Propose next week’s routine — you read the diff and tap Apply.
gym.landing.connected.never: It reads, it proposes, and it never rewrites a day you already have. That routine changes when you tap Apply on the diff — all of it or none — and never a moment before. A brand-new day it adds lands right away: it takes nothing away, and the day is yours to edit in Routines.
gym.landing.connected.levels: You decide what a connection may do — read, write, delete — and it can only see the tools for the levels you approved. Delete is never implied by write.
gym.landing.connected.coach: No agent of your own? Coach is a room in the app, over the same tools and the same rules — it reads your whole log and it proposes, and a change it writes is the same diff you tap Apply on. Every answer says what it read: which tools it called, and how many of your rows they served. It can’t log a set, correct one you lifted, or delete anything.
gym.landing.connected.levelRead: Read your log — sets, workouts, routines, records and notes
gym.landing.connected.levelWrite: Record what happened · add a new day or a new movement · propose changes to the days you have · share one workout by link · anybody holding that link reads it without signing in, for 30 days unless you end it sooner
gym.landing.connected.levelDelete: Discard a workout · end a share link · propose a removal
gym.landing.connected.neverGranted: This connection was never granted delete, so it cannot see the three tools that discard a workout, end a share link, or ask to remove a routine.
gym.landing.connected.precondition: Needs an AI tool of your own that speaks MCP — Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or any other MCP client. If you haven’t got one, this one is not for you yet, and the log stays free regardless.
gym.landing.exchange.asked: “Look at my last twelve weeks of bench. Write me a four-week block — heavier triples, and swap the flies for incline work.”
gym.landing.exchange.landed: A proposal on Push A. You read the diff, you tap Apply, you train.
